answer: In an agent market for opal trading, every identity must lock a bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Creating aliases is easy, but each alias needs its own bond, so a swarm ties up capital in proportion to its size and pays the opportunity cost for a month. This makes the market a poor haven for cheap sybils: the fable that one operator can gain unlimited bidding power merely by minting names fails when every name requires funds.
